gap: No result ChatGPT got states which GPS mount and hardwire kit each sub-$100 3-channel camera takes and what the maker charges for them: the Vantrue OnDash N4 ($99.99) needs Vantrue's USB-C GPS mount ($21.99) for GPS and a $29.99-$34.99 N4-named hardwire kit for parking mode, and the Redtiger A3 ($72.74) needs a $35.99 Redtiger kit, so neither stays under $100 once parking mode is added.
standout_why: Compared against six result pages opened 2026-11-26. my-best (us.my-best.com/22269) already says the N4 needs a separate GPS mount, takes cards up to 256 GB and has no app, but it gives no mount price, no hardwire kit, and quotes a $259.99 reference price. deal.ai lists the N4 at $99.99 and the A3 at $72.74 with no hardwire, GPS or card detail. Digital Camera World (cited) has no 3-channel camera and only says hardwiring is required on single-channel Nextbase models. cabincommand and dashanddrive name kits only for 70mai, Juscar and Vantrue E1-class cameras; dashanddrive estimates 'another $20 to $30' for a kit. None of them matches a kit or mount to the N4 or A3 by the maker's compatibility list or gives the all-in total. The need for a GPS mount is therefore already out there; the pairing, prices and totals are new.
decides: It confirms the OnDash N4 belongs on the page only as the bare camera at $99.99: with GPS it is $121.98, with the cheapest N4-named hardwire kit $129.98, with both $151.97. The Redtiger A3 at $72.74 keeps $27.25 of headroom, but Redtiger's own kit ($35.99) takes it to $108.73, so no row is under $100 with the maker's parking-mode kit. The N4 against A3 ranking on recording specs is unchanged; the page should state the add-on cost on both rows and name the Nexus 4S ($199.99, GPS built in) as the step-up for shoppers who want GPS without a mount.

findings.label: Price at Vantrue's US store
findings.note: Read from the store's own listing data through storecheck search; the product page itself returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so only the first ~1,500 characters of the listing were read. No sale end date was seen.

findings.label: Channels and recording with all three cameras
findings.value: 3 channels (front, cabin, rear): 1440P + 1080P + 1080P at 30 fps; front camera alone 4K 2160P at 25 fps; Sony STARVIS sensor; supercapacitor; 4 IR LEDs facing the cabin
findings.note: Vantrue's listing text. The headline feature list (4K single front, 3 channel, STARVIS, parking mode, supercapacitor, WDR, time lapse) names neither Wi-Fi nor GPS.

findings.label: GPS mount that fits, and price
findings.value: Vantrue Suction Cup GPS Mount, $21.99, in stock; the listing names 'Vantrue N4, T3 Dash Cam GPS Receiver Module Type C USB Port'
findings.note: The same listing also covers a Mini USB version for N2 Pro / N2 / T2 / X3 / N1 Pro / X4 / X1 / X2 / R2, so the buyer must pick the Type-C one. Location, speed and route are viewed in Vantrue Player (Windows and Mac). Arithmetic: $99.99 + $21.99 = $121.98. The variant list was not read (HTTP 429).

findings.label: Hardwire kits Vantrue names for the N4
findings.value: Voltage Display Hardwire Kit $29.99 (cutoff 11.6 / 12 / 12.4 V, names N4); 5-Level Adjustable 3-Lead ACC Hardwire Kit $34.99 (cutoff 11.6 / 11.9 / 12.2 / 12.5 V, timer 1 / 3 / 6 / 12 / 24 h or always, names N4)
findings.note: 5-level kit: https://www.vantrue.com/products/5-level-adjustable-hardwire-kit, which states 'It doesn't work for other Vantrue Dash Cams, it only work for N4 N5 N4 Pro and E1, E2, S2-2CH, S2-3CH, N2S, X4S, T3'. Both take 12-24 V vehicles and use USB Type-C. Arithmetic: N4 + voltage-display kit = $129.98; N4 + 5-level kit = $134.98; N4 + GPS mount + voltage-display kit = $151.97.

findings.label: Cheaper Vantrue kit, N4 not named in the text read
findings.value: Universal 11.5ft ACC Hardwire Kit $24.99 (list $29.99); USB Type-C; cutoff 11.6 V / 23.2 V; 'it only work for Vantrue dash cam'
findings.note: The listing text read does not list models, so N4 fit is by Vantrue's 'all Type C' wording only. Use the $29.99 kit as the sourced N4 pairing.
